report.headline: Bedroom 1: a ceiling section shows early signs of failing
report.summary: The review team opened 9 of 9 rooms, flagged 6 candidates, and an independent skeptic confirmed 5 and rejected 1. This is a screening of scan images, not an inspection.

findings.title: Rippled, raised ceiling finish with a lump beside the smoke alarm
findings.view_label: Bedroom 1, the ceiling, looking straight up (scan position R2-A)
findings.observation: Across a broad area of the ceiling the finish shows raised ridges and rippling, with a distinct rounded lump beside the smoke alarm. Dark spots line the ceiling-wall joint nearby.
findings.possible_consequence: If water is reaching this ceiling from above, the raised finish could sag further and a section could come away.
findings.verification: Raised ridges and a distinct lump beside the smoke alarm are clearly visible across the boxed area, and dark spots line the ceiling joint nearby. The second scan position shows a blistered, peeling patch on the same ceiling.

findings.title: Dark streaking on wall corner beside shower tile
findings.view_label: Bathroom, the view a quarter turn to the left of wall-1 (scan position R8-A)
findings.observation: Dark vertical streaks and spotting run down the upper wall in the corner directly beside the tiled shower surround.
findings.possible_consequence: If this corner stays damp from the shower, the wall finish could deteriorate and the darkening could spread.
findings.verification: Dark vertical streaks and spotting are clearly visible on the wall corner beside the shower tile. This bathroom was scanned from one position, so there is no second angle.

findings.title: Open crack running from the ceiling light fixture
findings.view_label: Kitchen 1, the ceiling, looking straight up (scan position R4-B)
findings.observation: A crack runs from the light fixture across the ceiling toward the wall, with a slight ridge along part of its length.
findings.possible_consequence: If the crack keeps opening, the ceiling finish along it could loosen.
findings.verification: A crack wider than a hairline runs from the light fixture, with a slight ridge along it. The second scan position's ceiling view does not frame this part of the ceiling clearly.

findings.title: Brown drip trails running down wall from ceiling line
findings.view_label: Bedroom 1, the view a quarter turn to the left of wall-1 (scan position R2-B)
findings.observation: Brown vertical streaks run down the upper part of the right-hand wall, starting below the ceiling line.
findings.possible_consequence: If these trails come from water running down inside or over the wall, the finish and the ceiling junction above could be getting wet repeatedly.
findings.verification: Brown vertical streaks run down from the ceiling line in the boxed area, and lighting or decor does not explain them. The matching view from the other scan position does not show this stretch of wall, so the ruling rests on one angle.

findings.title: Amber-brown stain on kitchen ceiling near wall
findings.view_label: Kitchen 1, the ceiling, looking straight up (scan position R4-A)
findings.observation: A soft-edged amber-brown discoloration with darker speckles spreads across the ceiling near the wall and the hatch.
findings.possible_consequence: If this stain marks water coming through from above, the ceiling finish here could be softening.
findings.verification: A soft-edged amber-brown discoloration is visible near the wall and hatch, and the second scan position shows the same staining near the hatch. In a kitchen, cooking residue could look similar, so confidence is low.

rejected.title: Blotchy discoloured patches on wall beside hallway door
rejected.reason: The patches have sharp, flat edges and an even lighter tone, typical of filler or spackle repairs painted over unevenly. There is no tide line, darkening or drip pattern, so patching explains them better than water.

scenario.title: A section of this ceiling could come down
scenario.premise: If the moisture source above this ceiling is not found and fixed
scenario.why: The finish here is rippled and raised over a broad area, with a lump beside the smoke alarm and dark spots along the nearby joint. If water is reaching this ceiling from above, the wetted finish could keep softening and lose its grip on the framing, and the raised area could sag further. A section that has lost its hold could come away.
early_warning_signs: Brown stains or rings appearing on this ceiling
The raised area getting larger or hanging lower
New cracks around the edge of the rippled area
A musty smell or dark spots spreading along the ceiling joints
scenario.recommended_action: Have the space above this ceiling checked for an active leak and the finish tested for moisture before any repair.
scenario.who_to_call: A licensed roofer or plumber to trace the water source, then a drywall or plaster contractor for the repair.

diy.label: Fix it yourself
diy.time: A weekend, plus drying time between coats

materials.name: 3M N95 sanding respirator, 2-pack
USG Sheetrock 1/2 in. x 2 ft. x 2 ft. drywall patch panel
USG Sheetrock All Purpose joint compound, 3.5 qt
FibaTape self-adhesive mesh joint tape, 1-7/8 in. x 150 ft.
KILZ Original stain-blocking primer, 1 qt
BEHR Premium Plus flat ceiling paint, 1 qt

steps: Fix the moisture source first, or the new patch will fail the same way.
Cut the loose finish back to sound material, squaring the opening so its edges land on framing.
Let the cavity dry, then screw a new board into the opening.
Tape the joints and apply two or three thin coats of compound, sanding lightly between coats.
Seal with stain-blocking primer, then paint to match.
cautions: The scan does not say when this home was built. If it predates 1978 the paint may contain lead, and older plaster or textured finishes can contain asbestos. Have the finish tested before you cut, scrape or sand it.
This is overhead work from a ladder. Wear eye protection, and get help lifting board into place.
Do-it-yourself covers the visible surface only. Finding and fixing the moisture source is a professional's job, and is priced on both sides.
At 13 sq ft this is a large patch. Most people hire a section this size out.

scenarios.title: This damp could spread and take the wall finish with it
scenarios.premise: If this wall keeps getting wet

Paint blistering or peeling nearby
A musty smell that lingers in the room

diy.time: An hour of work, then a day to dry

materials.name: 3M N95 sanding respirator, 2-pack
Concrobium Mold Control spray, 32 oz
KILZ Original stain-blocking primer, 1 qt
Interior paint matched to the wall, 1 qt

unpriced: Interior paint matched to the wall, 1 qt
steps: Wear an N95 respirator, goggles and long gloves, and ventilate the room.
Scrub the area with detergent and water, or a mould cleaner, and dry it completely.
Do not paint or caulk over mould: paint applied over a mouldy surface is likely to peel.
Once clean and dry, seal with primer and repaint.
Run the fan or open a window when showering, so the corner dries out between uses.
cautions: Dark streaking is not proof of mould, and images cannot confirm it. These steps follow the US EPA's guidance for cleaning a small area that may be mould.

The scan does not say when this home was built. If it predates 1978 the paint may contain lead, and older plaster or textured finishes can contain asbestos. Have the finish tested before you cut, scrape or sand it.
US EPA guidance treats mould under about 10 square feet as a job most people can handle. This region is 0.7 sq ft. Beyond that, or if it follows a lot of water damage, hire a remediation contractor.

scenarios.title: A section of this ceiling could come down
scenarios.premise: If this stain is water arriving from above, and its source is not found and fixed
scenarios.why: A stain like this can mark water arriving from above. If it is water and it keeps arriving, the finish under the stain could soften, sag and eventually let go. If it is surface residue instead, none of this applies, which is why the first step is to find out. The skeptic confirmed this at low confidence, so read what follows as a reason to check, not as a diagnosis.
early_warning_signs: The stain growing, or its edge darkening after rain or after water is used above
The stained area feeling soft or damp to the touch
The finish starting to sag or blister
scenarios.recommended_action: Press the stained area gently and check it with a moisture meter. A damp or soft reading means a leak to trace before any repainting.
scenarios.who_to_call: A licensed roofer or plumber if it is damp. A painter, or you, if it is dry and only stained.
